entries.title: Compiled Machine
entries.description: Run your own function; theorem cards certify every output

pages.title: Compiled Machine
pages.text:
A Compiled Machine runs one of your defined functions on numerals: a calculator you designed yourself. Its real power is the **theorem card**. With a proven statement about the function in its card slot, every output comes out *certified*, for just 1 extra energy unit. No searching on the Test Bench.

This is the payoff of proving: prove once that Double always gives an even number, and every Double you ever make is certified Even almost for free.

pages.title: How to use
pages.text:
**How to use**

- *Design: a circuit f(…)*: a circuit such as Double(n) or add(a, b). Only the function counts, not the variable names. At most 3 inputs.
- *Input 1*, *Input 2*, *Input 3*: numerals, in the order of f's inputs. Fill as many as f takes.
- *Theorem card*: optional, a statement about f.
- The output slot on the right.

Each run uses one numeral from each input; the design and the card stay. Energy: 1 unit per computing step, plus 1 for the card. The screen shows *Computes Double* and then *Computed 42 (… steps)*.

pages.title: Example
pages.text:
**Example**

Design: the circuit Double(n). Card: your theorem ∀n. Even(Double(n)) from the first proof. Input 1: the numeral 21.

Out comes 42, and its tooltip says *Certified: Even*. Put a stack of numerals in Input 1 and a hopper underneath, and you have an even-number factory.

Without a card the machine still computes, but its outputs carry no certificate. The outputs are always fresh numerals: certificates on the inputs are not copied over.

pages.title: Which cards fit
pages.text:
The card must end in a property of f applied to plain variables: Even(Double(n)), or Even(a) → Even(b) → Even(a + b) (→ means *implies*). The variables inside f(…) match the inputs in the same order.

**Typed ports**: conditions before the → must be met by certificates the inputs already carry. With design add(a, b) and that card, a certified-Even 4 in Input 1 and a certified-Even 6 in Input 2 give 10, *Certified: Even*. A plain 3 gives *Needs a certificate for Even(3)*, and nothing comes out. Conditions that are equations are simply computed.

pages.title: Other cards
pages.text:
- **Tested** statements work inside their tested range; outside it: *Inputs above the tested range (N)*.
- **Conjectural** cards work while their conjecture's block is powered. Each use runs a background check of the conjecture on those inputs, and a counterexample refutes it (see [Conjectures](entry://axiomatic:notebook/risk/conjectures)). Their certificates say *(conjectural)*.
- **Speed cards**: a fully proven f(x, y) = f(y, x), like a + b = b + a. It certifies nothing. Instead, for a function defined by recursion, the machine swaps the inputs to recurse on the smaller one: 3 + 2000 then takes a handful of steps instead of over 2000. Status: *Computed 2003 (… steps, inputs swapped by the card)*.

pages.title: Watch out
pages.text:
- *The card must be a proven statement with no open assumptions*: unproven (and untested) statements, and statements still stamped by an Assumption Chamber, are refused.
- *The card must conclude a property of Double(…) of plain variables*: the card is about another function, or about Double(S(n)) instead of Double(n).
- *Conjecture … is dormant: power its block*.
- *A symmetry card swaps inputs, so it must be fully proven (no conjectures)*.
- *Too big to search*: over 5 million steps in one run.
- Right-click the machine with a [](item://axiomatic:graph_lens) to read the definition it runs.
Copper, Circuit Boards and a block of redstone.

entries.title: Statement Conveyor
entries.description: Moves statements and circuits from machine to machine

pages.title: Statement Conveyor
pages.text:
Hoppers move numerals. The Statement Conveyor moves **statements and circuits**: one item every 8 ticks (2.5 a second) from the block behind it to the block in front of it. With it a factory can hand theorems and designs from machine to machine without you carrying them. It needs no energy.

Everything else (numerals, coal, dirt) is left where it is.

pages.title: How to use
pages.text:
**How to use**

- Place it while looking the way items should travel: the arrow on its front face points there.
- The block behind it is the source, the block in front the target: chests, barrels or machines.
- From a machine it takes only from output slots. Into a machine it puts items where a hopper would: the first input slot that accepts them.

**Example**: Witness Bench, conveyor, Compiled Machine in a row. Each theorem the Witness Bench proves rolls into the Compiled Machine's *Theorem card* slot (a circuit would go to its *Design* slot).

pages.title: Watch out
pages.text:
**Watch out**

- Placed the wrong way? Break it and place it again facing the other way.
- A full or unwilling target simply waits; nothing is lost.
- A card slot that already holds a different statement won't take another.

The recipe needs a proven ∀n. 0 + n = n (zero_add, from the Logic chapter), and crafting uses it up. Copy it first: the Duplicator copies a statement for 1 unit.
The scroll is a proven statement: ∀n. 0 + n = n (zero_add). Any variable name works.

entries.title: Certificate Sorter
entries.description: Splits numerals by whether they carry a certificate

pages.title: Certificate Sorter
pages.text:
The item filter of a factory. It splits a stream of numerals by one question: does this numeral carry a certificate for the property in the filter? Certified ones go one way, the rest the other. 1 energy per numeral.

It reads certificates; it does not compute. An 8 with no Even certificate counts as *not certified*, even though 8 is even. Certify first (Test Bench or a theorem card), then sort.

pages.title: How to use
pages.text:
**How to use**

- *Numeral*: the numerals to sort.
- *Filter: a property statement like Even(n)*: any statement of one property applied to one thing, proven or not; only the property's name counts. Make it on the Property Bench.
- *Certified (out below)*: a hopper under the sorter pulls these out.
- *Not certified (pushed out the sides)*: the sorter pushes these into a chest, barrel or hopper on any of its four sides.
- *Strict*: switches between *Sorts by Even (any cert.)* and *Sorts by Even (proven only)*. Strict treats *(conjectural)* certificates as not certified.

pages.title: Example
pages.text:
**Example**

Filter: the statement Even(n). A hopper below the sorter, a chest beside it. Put in two 6s certified Even and three plain 8s: the two 6s drop into the hopper, the three 8s are pushed into the chest.

Turn on *Strict* to keep conjectural numerals out of a line that feeds recipes or machines you don't want at risk.

pages.title: Watch out
pages.text:
**Watch out**

- *Put a property statement like Even(n) in the filter slot*: the filter is empty or holds something else (an equation, a relation of two things).
- With no container beside it, the *Not certified* slot fills up and sorting stops.
- A hopper that feeds the side chest back into the sorter makes a loop: rejects go round forever at 1 unit per pass.
- Hoppers can't fill the filter slot; put it in by hand.
Iron, a hopper, comparators and a Circuit Board.

entries.title: Networks
entries.description: Survey your cables; a certified tree loses no energy

pages.title: Cables as a graph
pages.text:
Energy flows from the dynamo along Copper Cables, and each machine loses 2% of it for every cable on its way (at most half). Machines touching the dynamo lose nothing.

A **graph** is dots joined by lines. Your cables make one: the dots (nodes) are every cable and every machine touching one; the lines (edges) are every place two cables touch, or a cable touches a machine. A **tree** is a graph with no loops: exactly one route between any two nodes. On a tree there is no wasted route, and the mod rewards proving it.

pages.title: Counting a tree
pages.text:
You don't need to inspect every route: a connected graph is a tree exactly when it has one edge fewer than nodes. More generally, edges − nodes + 1 counts its independent cycles (loops).

The [](item://axiomatic:network_surveyor) counts both. If the cycles come to 0, the network is **certified a tree** and the dynamo sends energy over it without loss: *Burning (lossless tree network)*.

pages.title: Network Surveyor
pages.text:
**How to use**

- Place it touching a cable of the network. It runs on energy like any machine: 10 per node per survey.
- It surveys when placed, whenever you press *Survey*, and again every 10 seconds.
- The top line reads *Network: 5 nodes, 4 edges*. The status says *A tree (0 cycles): certified, lossless.* or *Not a tree: 1 independent cycles, energy is lost.*, then what it found about [couriers](entry://axiomatic:notebook/factory/couriers) and [phases](entry://axiomatic:notebook/factory/phases).

pages.title: Example
pages.text:
**Example**

A dynamo, two cables in a line, a Successor at the far end, and the Surveyor on top of the first cable. Nodes: 2 cables and 3 machines (dynamo, Successor, Surveyor) make 5. Edges: cable to cable, and each machine to its cable, make 4. One fewer: a tree, certified.

Now lay two more cables beside the first two, making a 2 × 2 square. That is 7 nodes and 7 edges: *Not a tree: 1 independent cycles, energy is lost.*

pages.title: Watch out
pages.text:
**Watch out**

- Any change (a cable or machine added or removed, a phase switched) voids the certificate until the next survey.
- A machine touching two cables of the same network closes a loop. So does a 2 × 2 block of cables.
- Each separate network the Surveyor touches is surveyed and certified on its own; the screen reports the first. The dynamo runs lossless only if every network it feeds is a certified tree.
- *Touch a cable network to survey it*: no cable next to the Surveyor.
Copper, a map, compasses and a Circuit Board.

entries.title: Phases
entries.description: Two-colour your cables for double-speed power

pages.title: Two phases
pages.text:
Every Copper Cable has a **phase**, A or B. Right-click a cable with an empty hand to switch it: *Cable phase A* (copper look) or *Cable phase B* (silver).

A network that uses both phases makes a claim: *no two touching cables share a phase*. In graph language that is a **two-colouring**: give every node one of two colours so that each edge joins different colours. Only cable-to-cable contacts count; machines don't take part.

pages.title: Alternating power
pages.text:
Once a [Network Surveyor](entry://axiomatic:notebook/factory/networks) confirms the claim, the dynamo runs **alternating power**: *Burning: alternating power (x2)*. It makes twice the energy per tick and burns fuel twice as fast, so a coal still gives 16,000, delivered in half the time. Busy machines that wait for energy get it twice as fast.

Not every network can be two-coloured. Going round a loop the colours must alternate, so a loop of odd length comes back to the same colour. Lines, trees and even loops (a 2 × 2 square) all work.

pages.title: Short circuit
pages.text:
Until the claim is checked, mixed phases are a short: *Short circuit! Mixed phases need a surveyed two-colouring*. The dynamo throws away its stored energy every second, and only machines touching the dynamo itself get power.

That includes the Surveyor: out on the cables it gets nothing. So place it touching **both** the dynamo and a cable of the network. If the colouring is wrong it says where: *; phases clash at x y z (odd cycle or same-phase neighbours)*.

pages.title: Example
pages.text:
**Example**

A dynamo with a phase A cable east of it, a phase B cable east of that leading to a Successor, and another B cable on top of the A cable. Put the Surveyor on top of the dynamo, touching that upper B cable. Each B touches only the A: certified, and the dynamo runs at x2.

Add one more B cable on top of the eastern B: it touches two B cables, the Surveyor reports a clash, and the dynamo shorts.

**Watch out**: switching any phase changes the network; it must be surveyed again.

entries.title: Couriers
entries.description: On an Eulerian network, deliver items to every machine

pages.title: Euler circuits
pages.text:
Can you draw a figure without lifting your pen, using every line exactly once and ending where you started? Euler answered it: yes exactly when the figure is connected and every dot has an even number of lines. Each visit to a dot uses one line in and one line out. Such a walk is an **Euler circuit**.

A courier that walks every cable exactly once passes every machine on the way, and needs a network where that walk exists.

pages.title: Eulerian networks
pages.text:
For couriers only the cables count: every cable must touch an even number of other cables (2, 4 or 6), and there must be at least 3 cables. A closed loop with no loose ends works. A dead end (one neighbour) or a T-junction (three) breaks it. Machines along the loop don't matter.

The Network Surveyor checks it on every survey: *Every cable has an even number of cable neighbours: Eulerian, certified for couriers.* or *Some cable has an odd number of cable neighbours.*

pages.title: Courier Station
pages.text:
**How to use**

- Place it touching a cable of the network, and have a Surveyor certify that network.
- Fill the three *Cargo for the machines on the network* slots with anything.
- Every half second it visits the next machine in turn and hands over one item that machine accepts, into the slot a hopper from above would fill. 1 energy per item.

The status reads *Delivering to N machines*, counting every machine on the network except the station itself.

pages.title: Example
pages.text:
**Example**

A ring of 8 cables around one block, with the Courier Station in the middle. On top of the ring: a Surveyor and a Successor. Every cable touches exactly two others: certified Eulerian. Put two numerals 4 in the cargo: both are delivered to the Successor, which counts them up.

**Watch out**

- *Needs a network surveyed as Eulerian: every cable joined to an even number of cables*: a loose end, or no survey since the last change.
- *No machine on the network takes this item*.
Copper, a minecart, hoppers and a Circuit Board.

entries.title: Automation
entries.description: Hoppers, other mods' pipes and power, and risk in factories

pages.title: Hoppers
pages.text:
Every machine works with hoppers. The rule: items go **into input slots** (and the dynamo's fuel slot), and come **out of output slots**.

- A hopper pointing into a machine, from above or from the side, puts each item into the first input slot that accepts it.
- A hopper underneath pulls finished items from the output slots. Inputs are never pulled out.
- The Coal Dynamo takes fuel from hoppers and gives back what burnt fuel leaves (empty buckets).

pages.title: The Certificate Sorter
pages.text:
The sorter has its own face rules:

- From above: into *Numeral* only.
- From the sides: into *Numeral*; pipes on the sides may also take from *Not certified*.
- From below: out of *Certified (out below)* only.
- The filter slot is filled by hand.

It also pushes its rejects into containers beside it by itself, so a plain chest beside it is enough.

pages.title: Watch out
pages.text:
**Watch out**: a hopper can't choose a slot; it fills the first one that takes the item.

- Compiled Machine: a circuit lands in *Design*, a statement in *Theorem card*, and numerals fill *Input 1*, then *Input 2* when Input 1 holds a different number. For two-input designs, feed by hand or keep the inputs in step.
- Test Bench: if the first slot holds a different numeral, the next one lands in the *Bound numeral (range mode)* slot.
- The Statement Conveyor and the Courier Station fill slots the same way a hopper above would.

pages.title: Other mods
pages.text:
Pipes from other mods follow the same rules as hoppers: they may insert into input slots and take from output slots, from any side (the sorter keeps its own face rules).

Generators from other mods can power any Axiomatic machine directly: **4 FE make 1 unit** of energy (the server option foreignEnergyPerUnit; 0 turns it off). Small trickles add up. Energy only goes in: you can't pull Axiomatic energy out to run other mods' machines, and the Coal Dynamo takes no FE.

pages.title: Risk in factories
pages.text:
Conjectural certificates travel. A recipe that accepts a certified numeral also accepts a *(conjectural)* one, and the result remembers it: a Circuit Board made from conjecturally certified evens shows *Depends on 1 unproven conjecture(s)*. Whatever you craft from that board, machines included, inherits the risk, and a machine keeps it when you break it and place it again.

If the conjecture is refuted, such a machine stops: *Built from parts resting on refuted …: it no longer works*. Risky items in your inventory turn into Paradox Junk. A *Strict* [Certificate Sorter](entry://axiomatic:notebook/factory/certificate_sorter) keeps conjectural numerals out of your crafting lines.
